Pilica New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Pilica, Poland

Not demolished. This, the newer of Pilica's Jewish cemeteries, was established in 1842 outside the town along the road to Kocikowo, on a site once known as 'The Blackwood Cemetery.' During WWII, the Germans devastated the cemetery, removing numerous tombstones and destroying its pre-burial house between 1943 and 1944; in 1942–43, Jews who had been hiding in neighboring villages were executed there. In 1945, after the war's end, the Wolbrom gendarmerie shot 70 people from Pilica at the cemetery. A 1884 architectural drawing for the cemetery's development and extension, created by the Olkusz County architect-engineer Karol Czaplicki, survives in the State Archive in Kielce.
